1.pericope_label: The vision of Obadiah. Thus saith the Lord GOD concerning Edom; We have heard a rumour from the LORD, and an ambassador is sent among the heathen, Arise ye, and let us rise up against her in battle
debates: Whether the smallness is a reproof already true or a punishment still coming
Why the heading announces a message instead of giving one
What the rumour is and who set it going
outliers: Ellicott allows that the second half of the heading may come from a later hand
Calvin takes the minority reading and says so, against the consent of nearly all
Clarke reports that no question about the prophet has ever received an answer worth recording
themes: A prophet known by nothing but his name
A rumour that turns out to be a command
A country no larger than an English county
Pride kept up in a narrow pass between mountains

3.pericope_label: The pride of thine heart hath deceived thee, thou that dwellest in the clefts of the rock, whose habitation is high; that saith in his heart, Who shall bring me down to the ground?
debates: What the word for their rock-dwellings means, and whether it names a city
Whether the boast rests on the caves or on the height
How much of their confidence was actually well founded
outliers: Calvin objects that clefts do not suit a city standing on a plain
Keil and Delitzsch traces the disputed word to a sense of refuge or asylum
Wesley has the stars fight in their courses when armies cannot be raised
themes: Subterranean dwellings hewn like ovens
A people who thought themselves beyond the reach of darts
A nest built among the stars
Defences God does not trouble to count

5.pericope_label: If thieves came to thee, if robbers by night, (how art thou cut off!) would they not have stolen till they had enough? All the men of thy confederacy have brought thee even to the border
debates: Whether it is fugitives or ambassadors who are sent back to the border
Whether the hidden things are treasures or hiding-places
Whether the last clause means a wound, an ambush, or a net
outliers: Keil and Delitzsch rejects the fugitive reading on the ground of a single suffix
Calvin says the alliance itself, not the mountains, was what ruined Edom
Ellicott makes the betrayal by allies the exact repayment of Edom’s own treachery
themes: Thieves who would at least have left something
Gleanings a grape-gatherer never troubles to take
Narrow passes conquerors usually avoid
Ambassadors escorted politely back to the frontier

8.pericope_label: Shall I not in that day, saith the LORD, even destroy the wise men out of Edom, and understanding out of the mount of Esau? And thy mighty men, O Teman, shall be dismayed
debates: Whether the wise men are killed or merely stripped of their wisdom
Whether Teman is a district, a city, or the point of the compass
Where the word for slaughter belongs in the sentence
outliers: Calvin names the Venetians of his own day as the standing example of self-admiring cunning
Keil and Delitzsch argues the point from the second clause naming only discernment
Calvin calls what looks like understanding and strength in men empty smoke
themes: Counsellors left with nothing to advise
A wisdom that is really insanity
Soldiers throwing away their arms
Gifts held in place only by the giver

10.pericope_label: For thy violence against thy brother Jacob shame shall cover thee, and thou shalt be cut off for ever. In the day that thou stoodest on the other side... even thou wast as one of them
debates: Whether Edom fought against Judah or merely stood by
Why one crime out of many is made to carry the whole sentence
Whether the plundered thing is forces or substance
outliers: Calvin says being cut off for ever proves Edom was never within the covenant it claimed
Ellicott reads Edom as a neutral waiting to join the winning side
Ellicott notes that Esau himself was generous where his descendants were not
themes: A redeemer who becomes the assailant
Circumcision claimed and profaned at once
Spectators taking pleasure in a mournful sight
Lots cast in the streets of a captured capital

12.pericope_label: But thou shouldest not have looked on the day of thy brother in the day that he became a stranger; neither shouldest thou have rejoiced over the children of Judah in the day of their destruction
debates: Whether the clauses are prohibitions or reproaches for what was already done
Whether the waiting place is a fork in the road or a breach in the wall
What it means that the brother became a stranger
outliers: Calvin dismisses one proposed sense of the crossway as too frigid
Calvin notes that only Edom knew the roads well enough to block every one
Clarke says rejoicing at a punishment makes the other man’s crime our own
themes: Eyes closed because they cannot help
Neighbours who came in with the besiegers
A nation whose very look had changed
Every road out watched by someone who knew it

15.pericope_label: For the day of the LORD is near upon all the heathen: as thou hast done, it shall be done unto thee: thy reward shall return upon thine own head
debates: Who drank on the holy mountain, the Jews in affliction or the Edomites in triumph
Whether the argument runs from the greater nations to the lesser or takes in all alike
How near the day actually was
outliers: Clarke says God will not let Edom stand beside him as an executioner of judgment
Calvin makes the second drinking a different act from the first
Gill dates the ruin of Edom about five years after the fall of Jerusalem
themes: A cup passed round the whole world
Punishment mistaken for proof of one’s own innocence
Feasting on a mountain that was not theirs
Plunderers who become the plunder

17.pericope_label: But upon mount Zion shall be deliverance, and there shall be holiness; and the house of Jacob shall possess their possessions
debates: Whether the possessions are Israel’s own or the lands of the nations
Whether the house of Jacob here means all Israel or Judah alone
Whether the first word names an act of rescue or the people rescued
outliers: Calvin notes the escape is promised in the mountain, not from it
Ellicott sets the parallelism against the reading of the old versions
Calvin observes that Edom fell while the exiles were slaves who could not lift a finger
themes: A mountain turned from drinking-hall back into sanctuary
A remedy prepared at the same time as the wound
Old inheritances handed back to those who lost them
Stubble set alight by a house that looked dead

19.pericope_label: And they of the south shall possess the mount of Esau... And saviours shall come up on mount Zion to judge the mount of Esau; and the kingdom shall be the LORD’S
debates: Where Sepharad was, if it can be placed at all
Whether the saviours are the returning leaders, the Maccabees, or the apostles
Whether the promised borders were ever actually held
outliers: Calvin says the grant to Abraham was never fulfilled because the people themselves obstructed it
Clarke reports manuscripts reading the preserved instead of saviours
Calvin argues from the plural that the Messiah stands alone above his own ministers
themes: A boundary line pushed out in all four directions
A town remembered for melting glass
A place-name nobody has been able to find
Deliverers who are never the deliverer
